@dataclass
class User:
    """Represents an application user and the items they own.

    Attributes:
        id: Unique integer identifier for the user.
        email: Email address used for login and contact.
        name: Display name of the user.
        active: Whether the account is enabled; inactive users cannot log in.
            Defaults to ``True``.
        item_ids: List of item IDs owned by the user. Defaults to an empty list.

    Methods:
        can_login: Return whether the user is permitted to log in.
        owns_item: Return whether the user owns a given item by ID.

    Example:
        >>> user = User(id=1, email="alice@example.com", name="Alice")
        >>> user.can_login()
        True
        >>> user.item_ids.append(42)
        >>> user.owns_item(42)
        True
        >>> user.owns_item(7)
        False
    """

    id: int
    email: str
    name: str
    active: bool = True
    item_ids: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)

    def can_login(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if the user is active and has a valid-looking email."""
        return self.active and "@" in self.email

    def owns_item(self, item_id: int) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if ``item_id`` appears in this user's ``item_ids``."""
        return item_id in self.item_ids

class User:
    """Represents an application user and the items they own.

    Attributes:
        id: Unique integer identifier for the user.
        email: Email address used for login and contact.
        name: Display name of the user.
        active: Whether the account is enabled; inactive users cannot log in.
            Defaults to ``True``.
        item_ids: List of item IDs owned by the user. Defaults to an empty list.

    Methods:
        can_login: Return whether the user is permitted to log in.
        owns_item: Return whether the user owns a given item by ID.

    Example:
        >>> user = User(id=1, email="alice@example.com", name="Alice")
        >>> user.can_login()
        True
        >>> user.item_ids.append(42)
        >>> user.owns_item(42)
        True
        >>> user.owns_item(7)
        False
    """

    id: int
    email: str
    name: str
    active: bool = True
    item_ids: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)

    def can_login(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if the user is active and has a valid-looking email."""
        return self.active and "@" in self.email

    def owns_item(self, item_id: int) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if ``item_id`` appears in this user's ``item_ids``."""
        return item_id in self.item_ids
